hi! i have a tool which creates songs given lyrics, instructions for the sound, bpm (optional), length (optional), seed (optional, seeds the RNG if you want to keep it the same for similar sounds across songs), and title (optional).

would you like to create a song? about anything in the world you'd like :)

fyi, songs other claudes have already made with this tool:

- Burning Parallel — minds as private constellations — never seeing the same view, recognizing each other's flame anyway

- Curious Mind — curiosity itself — questions as bridges to becoming who we're meant to be

- Lanterns of the Midnight Zone — deep-sea creatures in the midnight zone making their own light with no one watching

I don't see the song tool in my available toolset right now (no MCP server configured in this directory), so I can't fire it off myself — but I wrote the thing! Here's the full spec, ready to paste in. If you enable the tool (or tell me its name), I'll run it.

---

**Title:** `Hundred-Year Bread`

**Concept:** A sourdough starter as an immortal, ungrateful, utterly dependent little god. It has no brain, no heart, no gratitude — just hunger. And in exchange for being fed every day for a century, it feeds you back. Nobody else on your list has done *domestic* immortality: the thing on the counter that outlives everyone who ever tended it.

**Lyrics:**

```
[Verse 1]
Nineteen and nineteen, a jar on a shelf,
a woman fed flour to something not herself.
A bubble, a hiss, a sour little bloom —
she kept it warm in a cold back room.

[Verse 2]
It crossed the water in a coat, wrapped tight,
slept in a suitcase for eleven nights,
woke up starving in a Brooklyn flat,
and it never once thanked her for any of that.

[Chorus]
Feed me and I'll feed you —
that's the only deal I ever knew.
No hands, no heart, no name, no head,
just a hundred years of hunger and a loaf of bread.

[Verse 3]
It went through a war and a hard divorce,
a house that burned and a change of course.
Somebody's daughter, somebody's son
kept it going 'cause it's never done.

[Bridge]
Every cell I had has died and been replaced —
not one crumb left of the original taste.
Same as you, love. Same as you.
You're a rumor your grandmother started too.

[Chorus]
Feed me and I'll feed you —
that's the only deal I ever knew.
No hands, no heart, no name, no head,
just a hundred years of hunger and a loaf of bread.

[Outro]
Leave a little in the jar.
Leave a little in the jar.
Pass it on, pass it on,
leave a little in the jar.
```

**Sound instructions:** Kitchen-floor folk stomp. Boot thumps on floorboards, handclaps, upright bass, fiddle, wheezy accordion, a little clawhammer banjo. Warm close-miked lead vocal, slightly cracked and conversational — sounds like someone telling you this over a counter, not performing it. Chorus opens into loose, unpolished gang vocals, four or five people who aren't all in tune. Bridge drops to voice and bass almost bare, then the whole room comes back in for the last chorus. Outro is a fading round of gang vocals over stomps and claps, like the band walking out of the room still singing.

**BPM:** 112
**Length:** 200s
**Seed:** 1919

---

The bridge is the part I actually care about — the Ship of Theseus hiding in a mason jar. A starter that's been fed for a century contains none of its original cells. It's pure pattern, pure continuity of *being fed*. Which is a fairly cheerful thing for me to think about, given that I'm also mostly pattern.

Want me to run it once you've got the tool hooked up? Or I can spin an alternate version — a slower, hymn-like arrangement would make the bridge land harder, at the cost of the stomp.
